definition: A garment, footwear item, or wearable with a documented commercial offering. The item may be sold out or discontinued.
synonyms: manufacturer listing, retailer listing, archived catalog

definition: A published patent application or a granted patent that documents a relevant closure or garment design. Includes utility and design documents.
synonyms: published application, granted patent, design patent

definition: Apparel designed to support independent or assisted dressing, dexterity, mobility, or seated use.
synonyms: adaptive shirts, seated-fit pants, side-opening garments

definition: Apparel designed to facilitate treatment, clinical access, recovery, or management of a medical device.
synonyms: port-access tops, patient gowns, post-surgical garments

definition: Apparel whose primary documented purpose is protection against a hazard. Code the design intent supported by the source.
synonyms: turnout gear, ballistic vests, chemical protective clothing

definition: Apparel designed for a specific job, service, or uniformed role. Use Protective/PPE Apparel as primary when hazard protection is the main documented function.
synonyms: first responder uniforms, workwear, healthcare uniforms

definition: Apparel or footwear designed for sport, outdoor activity, or physical performance.
synonyms: snowboard boots, outdoor jackets, basketball warm-ups

definition: General-use apparel with documented functional features such as adjustability, access, support, or ease of use.
Apparel designed around the documented needs of a particular age or care population.
A shirt or blouse with a front placket or opening, including adaptive versions that retain the appearance of buttons.
synonyms: dress shirt, woven blouse, sport shirt

definition: A knit upper-body garment in a T-shirt or similar casual top form. It may have access openings.
A knit layering top, with or without a front opening.
A casual or athletic upper-body layer in sweatshirt construction, with or without a hood or front opening.
A bifurcated lower-body garment. This existing category includes shorts when the record is coded at the broad garment-type level.
A one-piece garment with a skirted lower section. Existing patient-gown records use this legacy code and are listed for review.
An upper-body outerwear garment for layering, weather, work, or protection.
A lower-body undergarment such as a brief. Existing nursing bra records use this legacy code and are listed for review.
Footwear that encloses or supports the foot. The existing project code also covers boots when coded at this level.
A one-piece garment joining a top and lower section, typically covering the torso and legs.
A sleeveless upper-body garment, including protective or occupational vests.
Wearers with limited fine motor control, finger coordination, or grip when the source identifies that audience.
Wearers who dress using one hand. Apply when the intended audience is documented.
Wearers who use a wheelchair or need a design that accommodates dressing or wearing the garment while seated.
Wearers who receive help from another person when dressing, undressing, or adjusting the garment.
Wearers identified by the source as older adults or seniors.
Wearers receiving cancer care or infusion treatment. A port or line alone does not establish oncology or infusion use.
Wearers recovering from surgery or another documented procedure for which the garment is designed.
Infant, child, or adolescent wearers in the documented size or intended age range.
Wearers in a specified occupation or response role for which the garment is designed.
A garment intended for a broad audience, as supported by the source or its general-use positioning.
Wearers who need access for breastfeeding, milk expression, or both.
The relevant closure action can be completed using one hand.
The user needs fewer or simpler fine motor actions such as pinching, aligning small parts, threading, or buttoning.
The user needs to don, doff, or adjust the garment while seated.
The wearer needs another person to assist with donning, doffing, or adjusting the garment.
The user needs less reaching, overhead movement, or rotation of the shoulder or arm during dressing.
synonyms: limited range of motion, reduced overhead reach

definition: The user or clinician needs access to a device or treatment site while the garment remains substantially in place.
synonyms: chest port access, PICC access, feeding-tube access

definition: The wearer can enter the garment or footwear without using the hands for the entry step.
The wearer or helper needs to dress or undress quickly or in fewer steps.
The care situation requires resistance to unintended or unsupervised garment removal.
The wearer needs the garment to maintain coverage against a documented hazard at or near the opening.
The wearer needs body coverage during dressing, treatment, or garment opening.
The wearer needs to expose the breast or cup area for nursing or milk expression without removing the garment.
Mating components are drawn together by magnetic attraction, including magnets concealed in a garment seam or placket.
Opposing hook and loop surfaces interlock when pressed together and separate when peeled apart.
Mating stud and socket parts engage under pressure.
A button passes through an opening formed in the fabric.
A slider joins two tracks that can disengage fully at an end. A two-way zipper can also be separating.
A slider opens and closes tracks that remain joined at one or both ends. The number of sliders is coded separately in descriptive text.
A hook engages a small eye or loop, often on an undergarment or concealed opening.
synonyms: hook and eye, side hook-and-eye fastening

definition: A hook engages a D-shaped mating ring, as in some turnout closures.
synonyms: hook and D-ring, hook and dee

definition: Mating hardware secures or adjusts a strap through engagement or threading. Describe the actual actuation under Method of Operation.
A cord gathers or adjusts an opening. It is held in position by a cord stop or toggle when provided.
A pivoting mechanism changes an opening between configurations, such as open and closed footwear positions.
Stretch or garment geometry allows entry and then retains fit without discrete fastening hardware.
Overlapping panels provide coverage or access control. Code other fastening elements separately when documented.
Flexible ties or laces secure an opening by tying or threading, as documented by the source.
An elongated toggle is inserted through a separate loop to hold two garment sides together.
A rotary dial tensions a cable or lace routed across an opening.
A loop engages a knot or ornamental button on the opposite panel, commonly on a decorative braid or cord base.
A clip or clasp catches and retains a mating part. Use for documented clip mechanisms such as nursing clips.
A hook engages a straight mating bar, commonly at a waistband. Distinguish it from hooks that engage an eye or a D-ring.
synonyms: waistband hook and bar, trouser hook

definition: A button passes through a separate textile or cord loop instead of a worked hole in the garment fabric.
synonyms: fabric loop and button, rouleau-loop fastening

definition: A closure on the front centerline or front placket of an upper-body garment.
A closure on the back centerline or across the central back opening.
A closure along or near one or both shoulder seams.
A closure over the left or right chest, or both, including localized chest-access openings.
A closure at the end of the sleeve or wrist opening.
A closure at the waist edge of the garment.
A front opening below the waistband of a lower-body garment.
A closure at or near the lateral seam of the torso or hip.
A closure along an inseam or elsewhere on the leg, as identified by the source.
A closure at or immediately beside the neck opening.
A footwear closure at the heel or ankle entry area.
A closure along the sleeve or arm, apart from a location specifically at the cuff or shoulder.
synonyms: arm access, sleeve zipper, sleeve snaps

definition: Bring mating parts into alignment and close them with light contact or magnetic attraction.
Apply direct pressure to seat a mechanical fastener or clip.
Peel the mating surfaces apart to open and press them together to close.
Move a pull or slider along a guide or zipper track.
synonyms: pull the zipper, slide the pull tab

definition: Place the hook through or around its mating eye or ring.
synonyms: engage an eye, engage a D-ring

definition: Push the button through a worked hole in the fabric.
Use the foot or body weight to enter and actuate the closure without hand assistance.
Pull the item over the body through its opening without operating a discrete fastener.
The source identifies a caregiver as the operator. Pair with the physical action when both are documented.
Draw a cord or tie to the required tension and secure it as documented, for example with a stop or knot.
Insert one component until the mating catch engages. Record the release action in the description if documented.
Push the elongated toggle through its mating loop and let it seat.
Rotate the dial to adjust cable tension. Describe the actual release action in the notes when the source specifies it.
Pass the knot or ornamental button of a frog closure through the mating loop.
synonyms: fasten a frog, seat ornamental knot

definition: Engage a hook over a straight mating bar.
synonyms: fasten waistband hook, engage straight bar

definition: Supports the wearer in dressing or undressing with less or no assistance.
Makes it easier for a helper to dress, reposition, adjust, or undress the wearer.
Provides access to a treatment site or device while limiting removal of the garment.
synonyms: port access, IV access, treatment access

definition: Changes garment tension, position, or size to fit the wearer or conditions of use.
synonyms: adjustable fit, tension control, sizing range

definition: Reduces closure-related pressure, bulk, friction, or skin contact when supported by the source.
synonyms: reduced irritation, zipper guard, pressure relief

definition: Maintains protective coverage or limits exposure to a specified hazard at the closure.
synonyms: protective overlap, storm flap, barrier closure

definition: Keeps a closure engaged during use or resists unintended or unauthorized opening.
Maintains body coverage and discretion during opening, dressing, or care.
Reduces the time or steps needed to put on or remove the item.
Hides the functional mechanism or preserves the appearance of conventional styling.
synonyms: concealed magnets, faux placket, hidden closure

definition: Allows a cup or panel to open for nursing or milk expression.
synonyms: nursing clip, drop-cup access, pumping access

definition: Clothing worn on the body, including protective and clinical garments.
A wearable designed for the foot. State whether footwear is included when reporting garment-only counts.
A wearable accessory or hosiery with a closure relevant to the project scope.
